program.title: Badminton Doubles Shoulder & Lower-Body Control – Week 1

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Intermediate badminton doubles player, 1 session/week, 60 min, gym + court. Mild shoulder soreness after smashes. Needs shoulder durability, trunk rotation, lower-body control, and calf capacity for court recovery.
primary_constraints: Mild shoulder soreness post-smash; avoid high-volume overhead or maximum-effort pressing early
Only 1 gym session/week; must prioritize transfer to doubles court demands
Intermediate level; ready for unilateral and anti-rotation work
sport_demands: Explosive acceleration and deceleration in lateral and diagonal directions
Overhead smashes with trunk rotation and shoulder stability
Single-leg landing and lunge mechanics under match pressure
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Foundation phase: build shoulder external rotation and scapular control, lower-body unilateral strength, trunk anti-rotation, and calf capacity. Avoid high-volume smash or jump drills until shoulder baseline is stable and pain-free.

weeks.theme: Shoulder stability, single-leg lunge control, and trunk stiffness

workouts.title: Shoulder Stability & Lower-Body Unilateral Strength
sport_transfer: Shoulder durability and external rotation reduce smash-related soreness
Single-leg lunge control improves court deceleration and directional changes
Anti-rotation strength stabilizes trunk during explosive lateral movement
workouts.why_this_session: Build shoulder resilience, single-leg control, and trunk stiffness to prepare for higher court-load and smash volume without symptom escalation.

warmup.name: Wall Slide
warmup.purpose: Activate scapular muscles and establish overhead posture awareness

warmup.name: Forward Lunge Walk (Bodyweight)
warmup.purpose: Prepare lower-body mechanics and hip mobility for loaded lunges

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Activate core and reinforce pelvis/rib cage stacking before loaded work

main_work.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
main_work.purpose: Strengthen rotator cuff and improve shoulder external rotation control without load stress
main_work.load_guidance: Light dumbbell (2–5 kg) that allows full range without shoulder pinching or soreness
main_work.tempo: 2 sec up, 1 sec pause, 2 sec down

main_work.name: Forward Lunge
main_work.purpose: Train single-leg strength and controlled deceleration; build lunge mechanics for court movement
main_work.load_guidance: Light dumbbells (3–6 kg each) or bodyweight if form is shaky; prioritize clean front-shin control and depth over load
main_work.tempo: 2 sec down, 1 sec pause, 2 sec up

main_work.name: Half-Kneeling Landmine Press
main_work.purpose: Combine shoulder pressing with trunk anti-rotation and pelvis stiffness; shoulder-friendly angle
main_work.load_guidance: Light plate load (5–10 kg total); focus on stacked ribs/pelvis and smooth pressing path
main_work.tempo: 2 sec press, 1 sec pause at top, 2 sec lower

main_work.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Build unilateral ankle stability and calf capacity for single-leg landings and recovery
main_work.load_guidance: Bodyweight or light dumbbell (2–3 kg); use bench/wall for balance if needed
main_work.tempo: 1 sec up, 1 sec pause at top, 2 sec eccentric

cooldown.name: Calf Stretches
cooldown.purpose: Reduce calf tightness after loaded single-leg work

cooldown.name: Sleeper Stretch
cooldown.purpose: Address posterior shoulder and internal-rotation range without aggravating soreness

injury_modifications: If shoulder external rotation causes pain, reduce range and load by 50%; hold light isometric 3 sec x 5 reps instead
If front-knee lunge pain appears, switch to Lateral Lunge to train leg strength in a lower-pain direction
If calf soreness escalates, reduce reps to 5 and volume to 2 sets; prioritize pain-free range only

weeks.progression_rule: Establish pain-free shoulder external rotation and lunge mechanics; avoid smash overload. Monitor 24-hour soreness response; if stable, proceed to load increase in week 2.

program.nutrition_focus: Adequate protein (1.6–2 g/kg) for single-session recovery; timing flexible with 1 session/week. Support soft-tissue adaptation with micronutrient density.
recovery_focus: Monitor 24-hour soreness after session; mild pump acceptable, sharp pain or swelling = scale back load next week
Sleep 7+ hours; manage moderate stress with easy movement or mobility drills on off-days
safety_notes: Do not test 1RM overhead press or attempt max-effort smash drills in week 1; build baseline tolerance first
Shoulder soreness is mild and occasional; if it escalates to daily pain or limits movement, hold intensity and reassess
Lunge depth should respect anterior-knee comfort; stop short of pain rather than forcing full depth
assumptions: Athlete has access to light dumbbells, landmine setup, and bench at gym; court available for future skill work
No true injury or medical contraindication; soreness is training-related and reversible with conservative loading
Intermediate strength baseline allows unilateral patterns without extensive regression
1 session/week is the primary gym exposure; badminton practice and match play occur separately
